chapterTitle: Our Advocate, the New Commandment, and Remaining in Him
themeTitle: “This Is How We Know That We Know Him: If We Keep His Commandments”

scripture.text: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous.
scripture.understanding: τεκνία μου, “My little children” — τεκνίον, from the children family: a term of tender affection from an old pastor. ταῦτα γράφω ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ ἁμάρτητε, “I write these things to you so that you may not sin” — ἁμαρτάνω, from the sin family. Chapter 1 told them not to deny sin; now John tells them not to excuse it. καὶ ἐάν τις ἁμάρτῃ, παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα, “If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father” — παράκλητος, one called alongside: a defence advocate in court; Jesus calls the Spirit ‘another Counselor’ (John 14:16). Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν δίκαιον, “Jesus Christ, the righteous” — the only one qualified to plead our case.

scripture.text: And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὐτὸς ἱλασμός ἐστιν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, “And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins” — ἁμαρτία, from the sin family; ἱλασμός, from the offering family: the sacrifice that satisfies God's justice and turns away His wrath. Jesus is both Advocate and sacrifice: He pleads His own blood. οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων δὲ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου, “and not for ours only, but also for the whole world” — κόσμος, from the world family: the whole of humanity, not only John's readers or only Jews. How this relates to who is finally saved is debated among Christians; the verse plainly declares the sacrifice sufficient and offered for all.

scripture.text: This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐγνώκαμεν αὐτόν, “This is how we know that we know him” — γινώσκω twice, from the know family: knowing by experience, as distinct from οἶδα (vv. 20–21, 29), knowing as settled fact. The perfect tense ἐγνώκαμεν means a knowledge that has come and continues. ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν, “if we keep his commandments” — τηρέω, from the hold family: to guard carefully, to treasure. Obedience is the evidence of relationship (John 14:15).

scripture.text: One who says, “I know him,” and doesn’t keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him.
scripture.understanding: ὁ λέγων ὅτι Ἔγνωκα αὐτόν, “One who says, ‘I know him,’” — another slogan of the false teachers, who boasted of knowledge. γινώσκω, from the know family. καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ μὴ τηρῶν, “and doesn’t keep his commandments” — τηρέω, from the hold family. ψεύστης ἐστίν, “is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him.” Knowledge without obedience is self-deception.

scripture.text: But whoever keeps his word, God’s love has most certainly been perfected in him. This is how we know that we are in him:
scripture.understanding: ὃς δ᾽ ἂν τηρῇ αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον, “But whoever keeps his word” — τηρέω, from the hold family; λόγος, from the word family: the whole of what He has said. ἀληθῶς ἐν τούτῳ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ τετελείωται, “God’s love has most certainly been perfected in him” — ἀγάπη, from the love family; τελειόω, from the perfect family: brought to its goal, matured. God's love reaches its purpose when it produces obedience. ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐσμεν, “This is how we know that we are in him” — γινώσκω again, from the know family.

scripture.text: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.
scripture.understanding: ὁ λέγων ἐν αὐτῷ μένειν, “he who says he remains in him” — μένω, to remain, abide, stay: John's great word, used over twenty times in this letter. ὀφείλει καθὼς ἐκεῖνος περιεπάτησεν καὶ αὐτὸς οὕτως περιπατεῖν, “ought himself also to walk just like he walked” — ὀφείλω, to owe, to be obligated; περιπατέω, to walk, to live day by day. The standard is not a rule but a Person (John 13:15).

scripture.text: Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.
scripture.understanding: ἀδελφοί, “Brothers” — many manuscripts read ἀγαπητοί, ‘beloved’. οὐκ ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν, “I write no new commandment to you” — καινός, from the new family: new in kind. ἀλλ᾽ ἐντολὴν παλαιάν ἣν εἴχετε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, “but an old commandment which you had from the beginning” — παλαιός, old, long-standing; ἀρχή, beginning: the command to love was part of the gospel they first heard. ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ παλαιά ἐστιν ὁ λόγος ὃν ἠκούσατε, “The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning” — λόγος, from the word family.

scripture.text: Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you; because the darkness is passing away, and the true light already shines.
scripture.understanding: πάλιν ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν, “Again, I write a new commandment to you” — καινός, from the new family. The same command is old (they have always known it) and new (Jesus filled it with new meaning: ‘as I have loved you’, John 13:34). ὅ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν, “which is true in him and in you” — first lived out by Jesus, now by them. ὅτι ἡ σκοτία παράγεται καὶ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἤδη φαίνει, “because the darkness is passing away, and the true light already shines” — σκοτία, from the darkness family; παράγω, to pass by, like a parade going past; ἀληθινός, genuine, real; φαίνω, from the appear family: to shine. The new age has dawned.

scripture.text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now.
scripture.understanding: ὁ λέγων ἐν τῷ φωτὶ εἶναι καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῶν, “He who says he is in the light and hates his brother” — μισέω, to hate, to be hostile, or simply to refuse love. ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἐστὶν ἕως ἄρτι, “is in the darkness even until now” — σκοτία, from the darkness family. Spiritual claims are tested by how we treat people.

scripture.text: He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him.
scripture.understanding: ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ φωτὶ μένει, “He who loves his brother remains in the light” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family; μένω, to remain. καὶ σκάνδαλον ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν, “and there is no occasion for stumbling in him” — σκάνδαλον, the trigger of a trap, a stumbling block: love removes what trips up both the lover and others.

scripture.text: But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
scripture.understanding: ὁ δὲ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἐστίν, “But he who hates his brother is in the darkness” — σκοτία, from the darkness family, three times in this verse. “and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going” — εἴδω, from the know family (and the see family): he cannot see. ὅτι ἡ σκοτία ἐτύφλωσεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, “because the darkness has blinded his eyes” — τυφλόω, to blind. Hatred does not only keep you in the dark; it destroys your ability to see.

scripture.text: I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.
scripture.understanding: γράφω ὑμῖν, τεκνία, “I write to you, little children” — τεκνίον, from the children family: all believers, as God's dear children. ὅτι ἀφέωνται ὑμῖν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι διὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, “because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake” — ἀφίημι, perfect tense: forgiven and staying forgiven; ἁμαρτία, from the sin family; ὄνομα, His name, His person and work. Assurance begins with forgiveness.

scripture.text: I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, little children, because you know the Father.
scripture.understanding: “I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning” — πατέρες, mature believers; γινώσκω, from the know family: a deep, long acquaintance with Christ. “I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one” — νεανίσκος, young men in their strength; νικάω, to conquer; πονηρός, from the evil family: ‘the evil one’, the devil himself. γράφω ὑμῖν, παιδία, “I write to you, little children” — παιδίον, the second word of the children family: young ones still learning, as distinct from τεκνία in verse 12. “because you know the Father” — even the newest believer knows God as Father.

scripture.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
scripture.understanding: ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, πατέρες, “I have written to you, fathers” — John repeats with a change of tense. “because you know him who is from the beginning” — γινώσκω, from the know family. “I have written to you, young men, because you are strong” — ἰσχυρός, from the power family: having inherent strength, as distinct from δύναμις, ability in action. καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν μένει, “and the word of God remains in you” — λόγος, from the word family: the source of their strength. καὶ νενικήκατε τὸν πονηρόν, “and you have overcome the evil one” — πονηρός, from the evil family.

scripture.text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him.
scripture.understanding: μὴ ἀγαπᾶτε τὸν κόσμον μηδὲ τὰ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, “Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family; κόσμος, from the world family: human society organised in rebellion against God, not the earth itself or its people, whom God loves (John 3:16). ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν κόσμον, οὐκ ἔστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν αὐτῷ, “If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him” — ἀγάπη, from the love family. James said the same (James 4:4).

scripture.text: For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s.
scripture.understanding: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, “For all that is in the world” — κόσμος, from the world family. Three things: ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σαρκός, “the lust of the flesh” — sinful desires of the body; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν, “the lust of the eyes” — craving what we see; ἡ ἀλαζονεία τοῦ βίου, “and the pride of life” — ἀλαζονεία, boastful arrogance, the word of James 4:16; βίος, from the life family: the means of living, possessions, status, as distinct from ζωή (v. 25), the life of God. The same three appear in Eden and in the wilderness temptations. “isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s.”

scripture.text: The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ κόσμος παράγεται καὶ ἡ ἐπιθυμία αὐτοῦ, “The world is passing away with its lusts” — παράγω, the word of verse 8: the world is a parade already moving past; κόσμος, from the world family. ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, “but he who does God’s will remains forever” — θέλημα, God's will; μένω, to remain; αἰών, in the time family and the world family: into the age, forever.

scripture.text: Little children, these are the end times, and as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. By this we know that it is the final hour.
scripture.understanding: παιδία, ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν, “Little children, these are the end times” — παιδίον, from the children family; literally ‘it is the last hour’: ὥρα, from the time family: an hour, a decisive moment, as distinct from χρόνος, a span of time. Since Christ's coming, history has been in its final hour. καὶ καθὼς ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἀντίχριστος ἔρχεται, “and as you heard that the Antichrist is coming” — ἀντίχριστος, one who opposes Christ and takes His place; a word used in the Bible only by John. “even now many antichrists have arisen. By this we know that it is the final hour” — γινώσκω, from the know family; ὥρα again. The spirit of antichrist is already at work.

scripture.text: They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us. But they left, that they might be revealed that none of them belong to us.
scripture.understanding: ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθαν, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν, “They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us” — ἐξέρχομαι, to go out: the false teachers had left the church. “for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us” — μένω, the ‘remain’ of the letter, here rendered ‘continued’. “But they left, that they might be revealed that none of them belong to us” — φανερόω, from the appear family: made visible. Their departure exposed what they had always been.

scripture.text: You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all have knowledge.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου, “You have an anointing from the Holy One” — χρῖσμα, the anointing oil, here the Holy Spirit Himself, given by Christ (the ‘Anointed One’). The false teachers claimed special enlightenment; John says every believer has the anointing. καὶ οἴδατε πάντες, “and you all have knowledge” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family, since its root means ‘to see’): knowledge as a settled possession. The WEB follows manuscripts reading ‘you all know’; others read ‘you know all things’.

scripture.text: I have not written to you because you don’t know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth.
scripture.understanding: οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, “I have not written to you because you don’t know the truth” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family, since its root means ‘to see’). ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι οἴδατε αὐτήν, “but because you know it” — John writes to confirm, not to inform. καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἔστιν, “and because no lie is of the truth” — ψεῦδος, a lie: truth and lies have different fathers (John 8:44).

scripture.text: Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son.
scripture.understanding: τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύστης εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀρνούμενος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Χριστός, “Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ?” — ἀρνέομαι, to deny, disown: the false teachers denied that the man Jesus was the divine Christ. οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἀντίχριστος, “This is the Antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son.” — ἀντίχριστος; to deny the Son is to deny the Father who sent Him.

scripture.text: Whoever denies the Son, the same doesn’t have the Father. He who confesses the Son has the Father also.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει, “Whoever denies the Son, the same doesn’t have the Father” — no one can have God while rejecting Jesus. ὁ ὁμολογῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει, “He who confesses the Son has the Father also” — ὁμολογέω, to confess, to say the same: the confession of 1:9 now about Christ.

scripture.text: Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning. If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son, and in the Father.
scripture.understanding: ὑμεῖς ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω, “Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning” — ἀρχή, the beginning of their faith; μένω three times in this verse. The defence against new teaching is the original gospel. “If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son, and in the Father.” If the truth remains in you, you remain in God.

scripture.text: This is the promise which he promised us, the eternal life.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἣν αὐτὸς ἐπηγγείλατο ἡμῖν, “This is the promise which he promised us” — ἐπαγγελία and ἐπαγγέλλομαι. τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον, “the eternal life” — ζωή, from the life family: the life of God, as distinct from βίος in verse 16, the possessions and status of this life; αἰώνιος, from the time family.

scripture.text: These things I have written to you concerning those who would lead you astray.
scripture.understanding: ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν περὶ τῶν πλανώντων ὑμᾶς, “These things I have written to you concerning those who would lead you astray” — πλανάω, to lead astray, to deceive, as in 1:8. The false teachers were still trying to draw believers away.

scripture.text: As for you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you, and you don’t need for anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you concerning all things, and is true, and is no lie, and even as it taught you, you will remain in him.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρῖσμα ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ μένει ἐν ὑμῖν, “As for you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you” — χρῖσμα, the Spirit; μένω. καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ἵνα τις διδάσκῃ ὑμᾶς, “and you don’t need for anyone to teach you” — not a rejection of all teachers (John himself is teaching them), but of the false teachers who claimed believers needed their special knowledge. The Spirit leads into all truth (John 16:13). διδάσκω, to teach; ἀληθής, true; ψεῦδος, a lie. “you will remain in him.”

scripture.text: Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness, and not be ashamed before him at his coming.
scripture.understanding: καὶ νῦν, τεκνία, μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ, “Now, little children, remain in him” — τεκνίον, from the children family; μένω. ἵνα ἐὰν φανερωθῇ σχῶμεν παρρησίαν, “that when he appears, we may have boldness” — φανερόω, from the appear family: His visible return; παρρησία, openness, confidence, freedom of speech. καὶ μὴ αἰσχυνθῶμεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ, “and not be ashamed before him at his coming” — αἰσχύνομαι, to shrink back in shame; παρουσία, His royal arrival, the word of 2 Peter 1:16 and 3:4.

scripture.text: If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.
scripture.understanding: ἐὰν εἰδῆτε ὅτι δίκαιός ἐστιν, “If you know that he is righteous” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family, since its root means ‘to see’): knowing as settled fact. γινώσκετε ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγέννηται, “you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him” — γινώσκω, also from the know family: recognise by experience. Two ‘know’ words side by side: because you know what God is like, you can recognise His children. γεννάω, from the birth family: perfect tense, has been born and remains so. Righteous living does not cause new birth; it shows it.

visualMeditations.title: The Advocate in the Courtroom
visualMeditations.image: Picture a courtroom. You stand in the dock, guilty; the evidence is overwhelming. The accuser lists every charge. Then a man rises to speak for you — the Judge's own Son. He does not deny the charges. He holds up His scarred hands and says, ‘I have paid for every one.’ The Judge nods. The case is closed.
visualMeditations.meaning: “If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous” (v. 1). “And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world” (v. 2). Jesus is both your defence lawyer and the payment for your guilt. When you sin, do not run from God; run to your Advocate.

visualMeditations.title: The Old Commandment Made New
visualMeditations.image: Picture an old road map, its folds worn, that every traveller has carried for generations. Then picture the same road at dawn, lit by a sunrise so bright that every turn and stone is visible for the first time. The road has not changed; the light has.
visualMeditations.meaning: The command to love is old — it was in the law and in the gospel from the beginning. But in Jesus it became new: “Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you; because the darkness is passing away, and the true light already shines” (v. 8). Hatred keeps a person in darkness and blinds their eyes (v. 11). Love walks in the full light of the new day.

visualMeditations.title: The Passing Parade
visualMeditations.image: Picture a glittering parade passing down a city street — floats of gold and silk, music, crowds cheering, celebrities waving. You are tempted to run and join it. But as you watch, you see that it is moving steadily away, around a corner, and beyond it the street is empty.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world” (v. 15). “For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s” (v. 16). “The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever” (v. 17). Do not give your heart to a parade that is already leaving.

visualMeditations.title: Standing Boldly at His Coming
visualMeditations.image: Picture a soldier who has stayed at his post through a long night while others deserted. At dawn the King arrives. Some of the deserters hide their faces in shame; the faithful soldier steps forward to greet his King with joy and confidence.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness, and not be ashamed before him at his coming” (v. 28). The secret of confidence on that day is remaining in Christ now — staying in the truth you heard from the beginning, keeping His word and loving His people.

structure.label: Our Advocate and Sacrifice (v. 1-2)
structure.body: John writes so that his children will not sin; but if anyone sins, Jesus Christ the Righteous is our Advocate with the Father and the atoning sacrifice for our sins and for the whole world.

structure.label: The Test of Obedience (v. 3-6)
structure.body: We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments; whoever claims to know Him but disobeys is a liar; in whoever keeps His word God's love is perfected; whoever claims to remain in Him must walk as Jesus walked.

structure.label: The Test of Love (v. 7-11)
structure.body: The command to love is old, yet new, because the darkness is passing and the true light is shining; whoever hates his brother is still in darkness and blinded, but whoever loves his brother remains in the light.

structure.label: Assurance for Every Stage (v. 12-14)
structure.body: John writes to little children whose sins are forgiven and who know the Father, to fathers who know Him who is from the beginning, and to young men who are strong, have God's word remaining in them and have overcome the evil one.

structure.label: Do Not Love the World (v. 15-17)
structure.body: Love for the world — the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life — excludes the Father's love; the world is passing away, but whoever does God's will remains forever.

structure.label: Antichrists and the Anointing (v. 18-29)
structure.body: It is the last hour and many antichrists have arisen, who went out from the church because they never belonged; believers have the anointing of the Holy One and know the truth; whoever denies the Son does not have the Father; let what they heard from the beginning remain in them, and remain in Christ so as to be confident at His coming; everyone who practises righteousness has been born of Him.

sections.heading: When We Sin: Our Advocate
paragraphs: Chapter 1 warned against denying sin. Chapter 2 begins by warning against excusing it: “My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin” (v. 1). Grace is never a licence. But John immediately adds comfort: “If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous.” The word παράκλητος describes a defence advocate who stands beside the accused. Jesus pleads for His people — not by denying their guilt, but by presenting His own sacrifice. Hebrews says, “he lives forever to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 7:25), and Paul asks, “Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us” (Romans 8:34).

That sacrifice is described with the word ἱλασμός: “And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins” (v. 2). It means a sacrifice that satisfies God's justice and turns away His holy wrath against sin — not by changing God's mind, but by God Himself providing the sacrifice. Paul uses a related word: God sent Christ “to be an atoning sacrifice, through faith in his blood” (Romans 3:25).

And its reach is universal: “not for ours only, but also for the whole world” (v. 2). John the Baptist called Jesus “the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29). Christians understand this differently in relation to who is finally saved; what the verse clearly declares is that Christ's sacrifice is sufficient for all, offered to all, and that there is no other.

sections.heading: How We Know That We Know Him
paragraphs: The false teachers claimed to know God in a special way. John gives the test: “This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments” (v. 3). Jesus said the same: “If you love me, keep my commandments” (John 14:15). Obedience is not the root of salvation but its fruit. A person who says ‘I know him’ while ignoring His commands “is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him” (v. 4).

Then John defines the standard: “he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked” (v. 6). The Christian life is not measured by a list but by a life: Jesus' own. And the command that sums up that life is love. It is old, because it was there from the beginning of their faith (v. 7); it is new, because Jesus filled it with fresh meaning — “A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another” (John 13:34) — and because the new age has dawned: “the darkness is passing away, and the true light already shines” (v. 8).

So love becomes the test of light. “He who says he is in the light and hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now” (v. 9). Hatred is not only wrong; it is blinding: “the darkness has blinded his eyes” (v. 11). You cannot see clearly — spiritually or relationally — while you nurse hatred. But “He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him” (v. 10).

sections.heading: Do Not Love the World
paragraphs: After assuring every group in the church — children, fathers and young men — that their sins are forgiven, that they know God and have overcome the evil one (vv. 12–14), John warns them: “Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him” (v. 15). The ‘world’ here is not creation or people, whom God loves, but the whole system of values and desires that leaves God out. Jesus said, “No one can serve two masters” (Matthew 6:24), and James, “friendship with the world is hostility toward God” (James 4:4).

John names the world's three appeals: “the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life” (v. 16). They are the same three that worked in Eden, when the fruit was good for food, a delight to the eyes and desirable to make one wise; and in the wilderness, where Jesus was tempted to satisfy His hunger, to seize the kingdoms He was shown, and to prove Himself by a spectacular leap (Matthew 4:1–11). Where Adam fell, Christ stood.

John's argument is simple: the world does not last. “The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever” (v. 17). To love what is passing is to invest in what will be lost. To do God's will is to share in what remains forever.

sections.heading: Antichrists, the Anointing and Remaining
paragraphs: “Little children, these are the end times” — literally ‘it is the last hour’ (v. 18). The church had been taught that the Antichrist would come, and Paul had described ‘the man of sin’ (2 Thessalonians 2:3). John says the spirit of antichrist is already at work: “even now many antichrists have arisen.” They are those who deny “that Jesus is the Christ” (v. 22) — who deny that the man Jesus is the eternal Son of God come in the flesh. And they came from inside the church: “They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us” (v. 19).

How are believers to stand? Not by seeking a new, secret knowledge, but by the anointing every believer already has: “You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all have knowledge” (v. 20). The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of truth who leads into all truth (John 16:13). And by holding to the original gospel: “Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning” (v. 24). New is not always better; in theology it is often worse.

The chapter ends with a call and a sign. The call: “Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness, and not be ashamed before him at his coming” (v. 28). The sign: “If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him” (v. 29). Right living does not create new birth; it reveals it. The family likeness shows.

ntConnection.heading: The Advocate, the New Commandment and the Overcomers
paragraphs: The Advocate (παράκλητος) of verse 1 is Jesus; in John's Gospel Jesus promises ‘another’ Advocate: “I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever” (John 14:16). So believers have an Advocate in heaven (the Son) and an Advocate within (the Spirit) — the ‘anointing’ of verses 20 and 27, of whom Jesus said, “he will teach you all things” (John 14:26).

Keeping His commandments is the language of the upper room: “One who has my commandments, and keeps them, that person is one who loves me” (John 14:21), and “If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love” (John 15:10). John is recalling what he heard at the supper where he leaned on Jesus' breast.

The young men who have overcome the evil one share the victory of their Lord, who said, “In the world you have oppression; but cheer up! I have overcome the world” (John 16:33). Revelation describes such overcomers: “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony” (Revelation 12:11). And the shame John warns against at Christ's coming echoes Jesus' own words: “For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him” (Mark 8:38).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “an intercessor, consoler.” παράκλητος, from παρά (beside) and καλέω (call), is one called alongside to help — especially a defence advocate in court. In John's Gospel it is used four times of the Holy Spirit; here it is used of Jesus, who stands before the Father on behalf of sinning believers. He does not plead their innocence; He pleads His own sacrifice. When you sin, the One who speaks for you is righteous, and He has already paid.

Strong's: “atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator.” ἱλασμός is the sacrifice that removes guilt and turns away God's righteous anger against sin. In the Greek Old Testament related words describe the mercy seat and the Day of Atonement. This study adds it to the offering family. John uses it twice: here of Christ's sacrifice for the whole world, and in 4:10 as the supreme proof of God's love. God Himself provided the sacrifice His justice required.

Strong's: “to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy).” μένω is John's signature word, used over twenty times in this letter and often in his Gospel (‘Remain in me, and I in you’, John 15:4). The WEB translates it ‘remain’, ‘continue’ (v. 19) and elsewhere ‘abide’ — but it is one Greek word. It describes a settled, ongoing relationship: Christ remaining in the believer and the believer in Christ, the word remaining in them, love remaining. The false teachers left; true believers remain.

Strong's: “an opponent of the Messiah.” ἀντίχριστος is found in the Bible only in John's letters. The prefix ἀντί can mean ‘against’ or ‘instead of’: an antichrist opposes Christ and puts something in His place. John knows the church expects a final Antichrist, but says that many antichrists have already come — anyone who denies that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh. The spirit of antichrist is not only future; it is present wherever Christ's person is denied.

Strong's: “an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit”. χρῖσμα comes from χρίω, to anoint, the root of Χριστός, ‘the Anointed One’. Every believer shares in Christ's anointing by receiving the Holy Spirit. The false teachers claimed an elite knowledge; John insists that all believers have the anointing and therefore all know the truth. The Spirit does not replace teachers, but He enables every believer to recognise the truth and reject the lie.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit is testing your knowledge of God by your obedience and your love — and calling you to remain in Christ.

items.title: Run to Your Advocate
items.body: When you sin, do you run away from God in shame, or run to Him because you have an Advocate? “If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous” (v. 1). The Spirit wants you to stop hiding and come straight to the Father, trusting the One who pleads His own blood for you.

items.title: Who Are You Not Loving?
items.body: “He who says he is in the light and hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now” (v. 9). Hatred is not always shouting; it can be coldness, avoidance, contempt or refusal to forgive. The Spirit brings a name to mind. Ask Him to show you how resentment has blinded your eyes (v. 11), and to give you love that walks in the light.

items.title: What Is Pulling Your Heart?
items.body: Is it the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes or the pride of life (v. 16)? Comfort, possessions, appearance, status, image? The Spirit reminds you that “The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever” (v. 17). Where is He asking you to let go of something that is passing?

audit.title: The Obedience Check
audit.body: Is there a command of Jesus you know but are not keeping (vv. 3–4)? Would someone watching your life say you walk as Jesus walked (v. 6)?

audit.title: The Love Check
audit.body: Is there anyone in your church or family you are avoiding, resenting or treating with contempt (vv. 9–11)? What would love in the light look like toward them?

audit.title: The World Check
audit.body: Which of the three — lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes, pride of life — pulls on you most (v. 16)? What are you investing in that is passing away?

practices.title: Walk as He Walked
practices.body: Choose one Gospel story this week — Jesus washing feet, touching a leper, welcoming children, forgiving from the cross. Ask: ‘How did He walk here?’ Then find one way to walk like that in your own situation this week (v. 6). Write down what you did and what you learned.

practices.title: Test What You Hear
practices.body: This month, whenever you encounter a new teaching or popular idea about God, ask three questions from this chapter: Does it confess that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God come in the flesh (v. 22)? Does it agree with what was taught from the beginning (v. 24)? Does it lead to obedience and love (vv. 3–11)?

prayerReflection: “Father, thank You that when I sin I have an Advocate with You, Jesus Christ the Righteous, and that He is the atoning sacrifice for my sins and for the whole world. Keep me from sin, and when I fall, bring me straight to Him. Let my knowledge of You show in obedience. Help me keep Your word and walk as Jesus walked, so that Your love is made complete in me. Search my heart for hatred, coldness or contempt toward any brother or sister, and lead me out of that darkness into the light of love. Thank You that my sins are forgiven for Your name's sake, that I know You as Father, and that in Christ I can overcome the evil one. Guard me from loving the world — the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life — for it is passing away. Thank You for the anointing of Your Spirit, who teaches me the truth. Keep me in the truth I heard from the beginning, and keep me remaining in Christ, so that when He appears I may stand with confidence and not shrink back in shame. In Jesus' name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
storyConnections.summary: On the night before He died, Jesus rose from supper, tied a towel around His waist, and washed His disciples' feet — including Peter's, and the feet of Judas who would betray Him. Then He said, “For I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you” (John 13:15). That same night He gave the new commandment: “A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another” (John 13:34). John was there, leaning on Jesus' breast. Decades later he writes that whoever remains in Him must walk as He walked.

storyConnections.title: Jesus Tempted in the Wilderness
storyConnections.summary: After forty days of fasting, Jesus was tempted three times. To turn stones into bread — the lust of the flesh. To gain all the kingdoms of the world and their glory — the lust of the eyes: “the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory” (Matthew 4:8). To throw Himself from the temple to prove who He was — the pride of life. Each time He answered with God's word and did the Father's will. Where Adam and Eve fell to the same three appeals in Eden, Jesus overcame — and so can those who remain in Him.

storyConnections.title: Judas Goes Out into the Night
storyConnections.summary: At the Last Supper, Jesus said one of the Twelve would betray Him. John, leaning against Jesus, asked who it was, and Jesus gave the bread to Judas. Then, John records, Judas “went out immediately. It was night.” Judas had walked with Jesus for three years, heard His teaching and seen His miracles, yet he did not belong. His going out revealed what he was. John writes of the false teachers in the same way: “They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us” (v. 19).
